rationale: The suffix -ness in Old English forms abstract nouns denoting a state or condition, and in this context "past" most likely refers to elapsed time or a former state of being, which aligns with past.n.01 ("the time that has elapsed"). The other candidates—a secret personal history (past.n.02) or a grammatical tense (past.n.03)—are too specific or anachronistic for an Old English abstract noun formation.
